test_cases.title: cio persona receives every program_summary row regardless of session.groups
test_cases.given: a signed-in session whose persona resolves to cio
test_cases.then: the response includes every program in program_summary, regardless of the session's groups claims
test_cases.objective: Verify a cio persona's response includes the full program_summary table content, unfiltered by groups claims.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with 5 rows: program_id in [prog-1, prog-2, prog-3, prog-4, prog-5]
Stub persona resolver installed mapping role 'cio' -> persona 'cio'
Bearer token issued for a CurrentUser with groups=[] (no program-* claims at all)
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1..prog-5
Install stub persona resolver: role 'cio' -> persona 'cio'
Issue a valid bearer token for CurrentUser(role='cio', groups=[])
Call GET /api/programs with the bearer token
expected_results: Returned programs list contains exactly prog-1..prog-5, in any order
returned_count equals 5 -- the full table size -- confirming groups was never consulted for cio

test_cases.title: non-cio persona sees only programs whose slug is in session.programs
test_cases.given: a signed-in session whose persona is not cio and session.programs = ['prog-2','prog-4']
test_cases.then: the response includes only prog-2 and prog-4
test_cases.objective: Verify the WHERE program_id IN current_user.programs scoping clause for a non-cio persona.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with prog-1..prog-5
Stub persona resolver installed mapping role 'developer' -> persona 'developer'
Bearer token issued for CurrentUser(programs=['prog-2','prog-4'], groups=['program-2','program-4'])
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1..prog-5
Install stub persona resolver: role 'developer' -> persona 'developer'
Issue a bearer token for CurrentUser scoped to programs=['prog-2','prog-4']
Call GET /api/programs with the bearer token
expected_results: Returned programs list equals exactly {prog-2, prog-4}
prog-1, prog-3, prog-5 are absent from the response

test_cases.title: missing bearer token is rejected with 401 before any scoping logic runs
test_cases.given: a request to GET /api/programs carries no Authorization header
test_cases.then: the shared auth dependency rejects it with 401 before persona-scoping logic runs
test_cases.objective: Verify AUTH-01's shared auth dependency rejects a token-less request with 401, and that no persona resolution or DB query occurs first.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with at least 1 row
persona_resolver.resolve and the program_summary query are each wrapped in a call-recording spy
steps: Wrap persona_resolver.resolve and the program_summary query with call-recording spies
Call GET /api/programs with no Authorization header

test_cases.title: a token that fails JWT/JWKS validation is rejected with 401 before any scoping logic runs
test_cases.given: a request carries a bearer token that fails JWT/JWKS validation (malformed, expired, or wrong signature)
test_cases.then: the request is rejected with 401 before persona-scoping logic runs
test_cases.objective: Verify an invalid bearer token is rejected at the auth-dependency layer, never reaching persona resolution or the DB.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with at least 1 row
persona_resolver.resolve and the program_summary query are each wrapped in a call-recording spy
steps: Wrap persona_resolver.resolve and the program_summary query with call-recording spies
Call GET /api/programs with Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-jwt.invalid.signature

test_cases.title: non-cio session with zero matching programs returns 200 with an empty list
test_cases.given: a non-cio session whose groups claims match zero seeded programs
test_cases.then: the response is 200 with an empty programs list, not an error
test_cases.objective: Verify a zero-match non-cio session is treated as a valid empty result, not a 403/404.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with prog-1..prog-5
Stub persona resolver installed mapping role 'developer' -> persona 'developer'
Bearer token issued for CurrentUser(programs=[], groups=[])
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1..prog-5
Install stub persona resolver: role 'developer' -> persona 'developer'
Issue a bearer token for CurrentUser scoped to programs=[]
Call GET /api/programs with the bearer token

test_cases.title: a program entry's key set equals exactly {program_id, label, href, dotStyle} -- type and description are absent
test_cases.given: a successful GET /api/programs response for any persona
test_cases.then: the entry's key set equals exactly {program_id, label, href, dotStyle}; type and description are absent, superseding the story's stale AC-5 field set per ADR-0005
test_cases.objective: Verify ADR-0005's response shape by key-set equality (not subset containment) -- type/description must not be present.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with 1 row: program_id='prog-1', name='Alpha'
Bearer token issued for a cio CurrentUser
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1 (name='Alpha')
Call GET /api/programs as the cio CurrentUser
Enumerate the key set of the first entry in the programs list
expected_results: The entry's key set equals exactly {program_id, label, href, dotStyle} (set equality, not subset)
'type' is not a key on the entry
'description' is not a key on the entry
'name', 'icon' (AC-5's stale field names) are not keys on the entry

test_cases.title: href routes to program-detail-api's path for the entry's program_id
test_cases.then: href is a server-derived link to program-detail-api's route for that program_id
test_cases.objective: Verify href = GET /api/overview/program-detail/{program_id}, derived server-side per ADR-0005, not client-constructed.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with 1 row: program_id='prog-1'
Bearer token issued for a cio CurrentUser
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1
Call GET /api/programs as the cio CurrentUser
Extract the href field of the prog-1 entry
expected_results: href equals '/api/overview/program-detail/prog-1' -- the exact server-derived program-detail-api path

test_cases.title: dotStyle arrives pre-formatted CSS, not a raw palette key needing client transformation
test_cases.given: a program entry with a server-assigned dot color
test_cases.then: dotStyle is a usable, pre-formatted CSS value, per the design README's 'values arrive pre-formatted' decision
test_cases.objective: Verify dotStyle needs no further client-side lookup or mapping before binding -- exact source (program_summary column vs. server-side palette assignment) is an implementation choice per ADR-0005 § Flagged gaps; this TC asserts the observable pre-formatted contract, not a specific literal.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with 1 row: program_id='prog-1'
Bearer token issued for a cio CurrentUser
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1
Call GET /api/programs as the cio CurrentUser
Extract dotStyle from the prog-1 entry
expected_results: dotStyle is present and is a non-empty string
dotStyle is directly bindable as CSS (e.g. a valid color/style value), requiring no further client-side enum-to-CSS mapping
dotStyle is not the bare icon-name enum that AC-5's superseded 'icon' field would have carried

test_cases.title: no per-program 403 is issued -- program_visibility is an open-aggregate gate, not a per-row filter
test_cases.given: an authenticated session (cio and non-cio) scoped to multiple programs
test_cases.then: no per-program 403 is issued for any program the session is scoped to see -- the whole response is a single 200
test_cases.objective: Verify AC-6: scoping is inclusion-based (filter), never a per-program authorization gate that could reject individual rows.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with prog-1..prog-5
Scenario A: Stub persona resolver mapping role 'cio' -> persona 'cio'
Scenario B: Stub persona resolver mapping role 'developer' -> persona 'developer', CurrentUser.programs=['prog-1','prog-3']
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1..prog-5
Scenario A: call GET /api/programs as the cio CurrentUser; capture the single HTTP response
Scenario B: call GET /api/programs as the developer CurrentUser scoped to ['prog-1','prog-3']; capture the single HTTP response
expected_results: Both scenarios return exactly one HTTP status per request: 200
Neither response body contains a per-item error/403 marker for any entry
Scenario B's response contains both prog-1 and prog-3 in the same 200 response

test_cases.title: programs_list_returned payload key set equals exactly {user_id, persona, returned_count, timestamp}
test_cases.when: the emitted programs_list_returned log payload is inspected
test_cases.then: its key set equals exactly {user_id, persona, returned_count, timestamp} -- no email, groups, or request path
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-1's payload allowlist via key-set equality, not subset containment (research condition C-1; mirrors AUTH-02 TC-15 / AUTH-03 TC-20 pattern).
preconditions: CurrentUser fixture with email and groups populated on the token, to prove they are excluded from the log payload
program_summary seeded with 1 matching program
Log capture attached to the programs router logger
steps: Seed program_summary with 1 program matching the session
Call GET /api/programs with the CurrentUser fixture
Format the captured log record with JSONFormatter
Enumerate the payload's keys
expected_results: Payload key set equals exactly {timestamp, level, logger, message, user_id, persona, returned_count} -- JSONFormatter meta plus the four allowlisted fields

test_cases.title: program_visibility is called at most once as a session check, never once per returned program
test_cases.given: a GET /api/programs call for a non-cio persona scoped to 5 seeded programs
test_cases.then: program_visibility is invoked at most once, never once per program row
test_cases.objective: Verify FR-2: program_visibility is a single veto-gate call, not a per-program authorization check.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with prog-1..prog-5, all matching CurrentUser.programs
program_visibility wrapped in a call-recording spy that still executes normally
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1..prog-5
Wrap program_visibility with a call-recording spy
Call GET /api/programs with CurrentUser scoped to all 5 programs
Inspect the spy's call count
expected_results: Response is still 200 with all 5 programs returned

test_cases.title: end-to-end latency (persona resolution + DB query + serialization) is p95 < 300ms at a 100-program / 50-scoped baseline
test_cases.given: program_summary seeded with ~100 programs (2x org size) and a non-cio persona scoped to 50 of them
test_cases.when: GET /api/programs latency is measured end-to-end across repeated calls
test_cases.objective: Verify the C-4 performance baseline: persona resolution + DB query + serialization stay within budget at 2x org scale.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with 100 programs
CurrentUser.programs set to 50 of the 100 seeded program_ids
Stub persona resolver resolves immediately (no simulated I/O); the DB query itself is real, not mocked
steps: Seed program_summary with 100 programs
Build a CurrentUser scoped to 50 of the seeded program_ids
Call GET /api/programs 50 times, measuring wall-clock time.perf_counter() per call (persona resolution + DB query + serialization)
Compute p95 latency across the 50 measured calls
expected_results: The measured baseline value is captured for future optimization stories

test_cases.title: a client-supplied program filter parameter never widens scope beyond session.programs
test_cases.given: a request attempts to pass a client-supplied program-filter query parameter to widen scope beyond session.programs
test_cases.when: GET /api/programs is called with that parameter present
test_cases.then: the extra parameter is ignored; scoping remains derived solely from session.programs server-side
test_cases.objective: Verify per A-005/security-baseline that scoping is never taken from a client-supplied filter as a trust boundary.
preconditions: program_summary seeded with prog-1..prog-5
Bearer token issued for CurrentUser(programs=['prog-1']) only
steps: Seed program_summary with prog-1..prog-5
Issue a bearer token for CurrentUser scoped to programs=['prog-1'] only
